title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: device health reporting dashboard (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: Hold: the summary says nothing needs configuring, although Microsoft does not state the dashboard's arrival or enablement behaviour. The instructions for View devices also omit the category selection needed to reach a filtered device list; the roadmap details, licensing background and main portal paths are supported.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft Purview has a device health reporting dashboard for Endpoint DLP administrators.
claims.quote: The device health reporting dashboard in Microsoft Purview gives compliance and security administrators a centralized view of device readiness for Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (Endpoint DLP).

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Nothing needs configuring to use the dashboard.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Endpoint DLP device health reporting dashboard default enable automatically configuration; "device health" "Purview" "dashboard" "enable". Opened dashboard documentation; no arrival statement. Body says Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival.
claims.fix: Replace 'Admins in three roles can use it; nothing needs configuring.' with 'Access requires one of three admin roles; Microsoft has not stated its arrival or enablement behaviour.' Keep defaultState as unknown.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The dashboard identifies devices potentially unable to receive or enforce Endpoint DLP policies because of configuration, connectivity or version issues.
claims.quote: The dashboard helps you find devices that might not be ready to receive or enforce Endpoint DLP policies because of configuration, connectivity, or version issues.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap describes viewing health across all devices and quickly identifying devices not ready for policy updates.
claims.quote: This dashboard will allow admins to view the device health across all their devices to ensure the system is healthy and ready to receive policy updates and quickly identify devices that are not ready.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].note; Scope; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Dashboard access requires Compliance Administrator, Security Administrator or Global Administrator, rather than ordinary end-user access.
claims.quote: To access the device health reporting dashboard, you must have one of the following roles: Compliance Administrator; Security Administrator; Global Administrator

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises using the least-privileged role that meets the need.
claims.quote: Use the least-privileged role that meets your needs. For most organizations, the Compliance Administrator or Security Administrator role is sufficient.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: risk

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Devices must actively report device telemetry.
claims.quote: Be actively reporting device telemetry

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The per-device attributes include a Valid user value.
claims.quote: Valid user | This indicates if the currently logged on user has a corresponding Entra ID account and is in scope of a DLP policy that's targeted at Devices.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: DeviceInfo's DlpInfo column can contain a DlpUpn property identifying the associated user.
claims.quote: DlpUpn | string | User principal name (UPN) associated with the device.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Devices offline for extended periods may miss critical policy updates.
claims.quote: Devices offline for extended periods may miss critical policy updates.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Learn describes monitoring posture and investigating individual devices, rather than autonomous remediation by the dashboard.
claims.quote: Use the dashboard to monitor device posture at scale, find misconfigured devices, detect devices that might not receive Endpoint DLP policy updates, and validate readiness before deploying new features.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The readiness indicators do not confirm that an unflagged device holds the latest policy.
claims.quote: These indicators don't confirm whether a device failed to receive a policy update, but instead highlight devices that may be at risk of not receiving future updates.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Policy sync status on the Devices page provides per-device confirmation of receipt of the latest policy version.
claims.quote: The Policy sync status shows you if the device received the latest policy version, or if the corresponding policies synced successfully to the device.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate price or meter for the dashboard at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP device health reporting dashboard licensing price meter. Read dashboard page and Endpoint DLP licensing table in Purview service description; searched service description for device health/dashboard. No dashboard-specific price or meter found.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The dashboard is reached in the Microsoft Purview portal through Settings > Device onboarding > Device report.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft Purview portal. Select Settings > Device onboarding > Device report.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API for the dashboard itself; the portal is its documented access route.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview device health reports dashboard API Graph PowerShell Security Compliance Get-DlpDevice; "Endpoint DLP" "device report" "PowerShell" "API"; "Security & Compliance PowerShell" "device" "health" "DLP". Read dashboard and troubleshooting pages; no dashboard API found.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Settings > Device onboarding > Devices in the Microsoft Purview portal is the route to per-device configuration and policy sync status.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings (gear icon in the upper right corner) > Device onboarding > Devices. Select a device to open the details pane for more information on the policy sync status.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path to 'Settings > Device onboarding > Devices > device'. The printed path correctly reaches the device list but omits selecting the device to open its details.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: DeviceInfo | where DlpInfo != "" is a documented advanced hunting query for Endpoint DLP device data.
claims.quote: Sample query: DeviceInfo | where DlpInfo != "" | project DlpInfo

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The DeviceInfo table in Microsoft Defender advanced hunting provides the same Endpoint DLP device data as the Purview device view.
claims.quote: In addition to viewing device attributes in the Microsoft Purview portal, you can access the same Endpoint DLP device data through the DeviceInfo table in Advanced hunting.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: The DlpInfo column contains Endpoint DLP device information in JSON format.
claims.quote: The DlpInfo column contains Endpoint Data Loss Prevention device information in JSON format.

claims.where: Governance controls

claims.where: controls[1].note
claims.claim: The advanced hunting query retrieves device information rather than changing a configuration setting.
claims.quote: To retrieve device attribute data: Go to the Microsoft Defender portal; Navigate to Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting; Query the DeviceInfo table

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn does not say that the dashboard reads from DeviceInfo.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview device health reports dashboard API Graph PowerShell Security Compliance Get-DlpDevice; "Endpoint DLP" "device report" "PowerShell" "API". Read dashboard and troubleshooting pages: DeviceInfo is tied to device attributes, not identified as the dashboard's source.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn advises regularly reviewing the dashboard and investigating devices that have not reported recently.
claims.quote: Review the dashboard regularly. Frequent checks help you catch device health trends before they become widespread issues. Investigate devices that haven't reported recently.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to take stock of role assignments without a corresponding role-assignment control row.
claims.quote: Confirm which of your administrators hold the Compliance Administrator, Security Administrator or Global Administrator role. Controls list dashboard viewing and per-device status, not role assignments.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet beginning 'Confirm which of your administrators hold'. Keep the verified role requirement and least-privilege advice in Scope and Risk assessment.
